svg.text: Views
Presenters
Controller
Interactor
Database
Protect from change by depending inward
if A should be protected from changes in B, B should depend on A: Controller
protected from Presenters, Presenters from Views, and the Interactor from anything
(Database, Controller, Presenters, Views); arrows point toward what we want to
protect
Level and protection
the Interactor holds the business rules, the highest-level policy, so it is the
most protected (central; the rest are peripheral); Controller is peripheral to the
Interactor but central to Presenters and Views; Views, lowest level, are least
protected
Directional control
much of the class complexity exists to point dependencies correctly:
FinancialDataGateway inverts the dependency from the Interactor to the Database;
the FinancialReportPresenter interface and the two View interfaces do the same
Information hiding
FinancialReportRequester stops the Controller knowing the Interactor's internals;
without it the Controller would depend transitively on the FinancialEntities,
violating 'do not depend on what you do not use' (see ISP and the Common Reuse
Principle)
